Trying to wear your favorite shoes, but they seem to have shrunk overnight? Do you feel a sense of heaviness and "fullness" in your feet during the evening? Congratulations, you have joined the "Edema Club," experienced by approximately 75% of pregnant women.

Swelling (edema) during pregnancy—specifically the accumulation of fluid in the ankles, feet, and fingers—is very common and usually harmless. However, this condition can sometimes be more than just a cosmetic issue; it can be a serious health signal.

In this article, we will explain the true causes of swelling, ways to get rid of it, and when you should consult a doctor immediately.Why do we "swell" during pregnancy?

Your body's water retention is actually a mechanism that works for the benefit of you and your baby. There are three main physiological reasons for the occurrence of edema:1. Increased blood and fluid volume

During pregnancy, the amount of blood and fluid in your body increases by approximately **50%**. This extra fluid is necessary for the baby's development and serves as a reserve to compensate for the blood you will lose during birth.2. Uterine pressure

As your baby grows, the uterus becomes heavier. This weight puts pressure on the large vein (**inferior vena cava**) that returns blood from the lower body to the heart. As a result, blood circulation slows down, and fluid leaks from the vessels into the tissues, accumulating in the legs.3. Hormonal changes

Increased levels of progesterone and estrogen hormones cause the body to retain salt and water (fluid retention).Interesting fact: Swelling is usually felt more at the end of the day or in hot weather. It typically decreases upon waking up in the morning.Normal edema or a Dangerous signal? (Preeclampsia)

In most cases, swelling is normal. However, sometimes it can be a sign of a serious condition called **Preeclampsia** (Pregnancy toxemia).

**When to see a doctor immediately?**  - **Sudden swelling:** If your face or hands swell suddenly and severely within one day.
  - **Single leg:** If only one leg is swollen, red, and painful (risk of Deep Vein Thrombosis).
  - **Headache and vision disturbances:** If swelling is accompanied by a severe headache, "floaters" in front of the eyes, or blurred vision.
  - **Abdominal pain:** Sharp pain under the ribs.These symptoms can be indicators of preeclampsia accompanied by high blood pressure and require urgent intervention.7 effective ways to reduce edema

If the swelling is physiological, while it may not be possible to eliminate it completely, it can be alleviated.1. Drink more water (Yes, you read that right!)

Though it may seem counterintuitive, drinking water helps flush excess fluid from the body. When the body is dehydrated, it "panics" and stores water as a reserve. Drinking plenty of water (8-10 glasses a day) keeps the kidneys working and washes away toxins.2. Reduce salt, but don't cut it out completely

Salt (sodium) retains water in the body.  - **Avoid:** Pickles (salted cucumber, tomato), brines, chips, salty crackers, and canned goods.
  - **Caution:** You should not cut out salt entirely because iodized salt is important for the baby. Simply reduce the amount and do not sprinkle extra salt on food at the table.3. Sleep on your left side

Lying on your left side while sleeping relieves the "inferior vena cava" from the pressure of the uterus. This improves blood circulation and makes the kidneys' job easier.4. Elevate your legs

Whenever you find the opportunity during the day, and especially in the evenings, raise your legs above heart level. Lie on the sofa and put a pillow under your feet or lean your legs against the wall. Gravity will help the fluid return.5. Cabbage leaf compress (Grandmother's method)

For a natural cooling effect, you can wrap chilled cabbage leaves from the refrigerator around your swollen legs. This reduces the sensation of pain and heat.6. Comfortable shoes and socks  - Completely avoid high-heeled shoes.
  - Do not wear socks with tight elastic that constrict your legs.
  - If your doctor recommends them, wear **compression stockings (varicose vein socks)**. They should be put on in the morning before getting out of bed.7. Stay active

Do not stay in the same position (sitting or standing) for long periods.  - If you work in an office, get up and walk every hour.
  - Rotate your ankles in circular motions.
  - Swimming or walking in water is the best exercise for edema due to the water pressure.Nutrition: Natural remedies to fight edema

Some foods have a natural diuretic effect and can reduce swelling:  - **Potassium-rich foods:** Bananas, apricots (dried apricots), potatoes (baked with skin), spinach.
  - **Natural diuretics:** Cucumber, watermelon (in season), celery, parsley (in small amounts).
  - **Protein:** A lack of protein (meat, eggs, legumes) in the diet can also cause edema.Having "elephant feet" during pregnancy is no one's dream, but it is a temporary condition. Shortly after birth (usually within the first 1-2 weeks), your body will rapidly shed that excess fluid, and you will be able to wear your old shoes again.

Use the **Anacan app** to track your weight gain and swelling symptoms. If the scale shows a sudden increase, this could be a sign of hidden edema—inform your doctor immediately.
